primary.finding: N129 circular rim/hub with a flattened lower edge is the clearest wheel construction. Thick lower rubber mass still looks like a pedestal/dial base, and side tear weak at24. N127 tallring reads dial/plaque; N128 tread channels read an hourglass/lattice rather than rubber. Native diversity is ring/plinth versus treadblock; N127/N129 partially collapse.
primary.improvement: Q-tail removed; flat tire semantics unresolved.

independence.priorAwareness: Requested families and brief author design-feature summary known; not a fully blind recognition study.

technicalValidation.scope: Hashes and actual native24 mask comparisons only; producer handles full export-budget verification.

visualRecommendation.reason: Two meanings remain unresolved; smooth antialiasing conflicts with the bound historical pixel-discipline rubric. No formal score or deterministic go invented.
visualRecommendation.direction: Six of eight new family candidates are provisionally stronger; two remain diagnostic.

selected.finding: Static bent-over body, lowered head and forearm across thighs read exertion/rest at24 and32. Removes walking stride and establishes shared bodily vocabulary with N124.
selected.strongestObjection: Can mean injury or catching breath; campaign fatigue is contextual, not a universal pictogram.

selected.finding: Seated/slumped torso and extended bent legs clearly lower the body compared with N123. Head/torso/legs remain distinguishable at24; more clearly human than N125/N126.
selected.strongestObjection: Could mean injured or resting; strongest when learned alongside the standing tired pose.

selected.finding: Flattened lower bulge is visible, but tall ring and hub also resemble bell/bottle/marker. Tire identity insufficiently secure at24.
selected.strongestObjection: Deflation is plausible only after label disclosure. Do not mark family resolved.

selected.finding: Ship/water context removes the prior pistol collision. Detached canted underwater appendage is visible, but exact rudder versus other appendage/propulsion remains uncertain.
selected.strongestObjection: Core steering identity remains ambiguous; naval context alone does not close it.

selected.finding: Ship over downward widening signal fronts with cancellation slash communicates disabled underwater sensing. More coherent than the prior anchor/cross.
selected.strongestObjection: Arcs are symbolic and require naval context; must remain distinct from radar dish and generic communications.

selected.finding: Wave occupies the visible hull interior and crosses the vessel; conveys water inside a ship, clearer than arrow/transfer N136.
selected.strongestObjection: Ordinary vessel-in-water remains a secondary reading; tiny down-arrow is not reliably identified at24 and cannot carry the meaning.

selected.finding: Helmet plus one downward chevron remains clean at24/32 and distinct from two-chevron N140. Appropriate shared minor-pressure vocabulary.
selected.strongestObjection: Severity convention is learned. Keep explicit Daisenjutsu state mapping; do not imply Omega semantics are identical.

selected.finding: Two downward chevrons remain separate above the helmet at24 and give a clear next pressure tier.
selected.strongestObjection: Helmet occupies less optical area than the human poses; spacing/weight must be checked as a complete set. Do not reuse this ladder for Panicked without a separate decision.

notSelected.reason: Resting/leaning interpretation but inferior to N123; support/cane or stride ambiguity remains.
Frontal shoulder arch reads clothing rather than bodily fatigue.
Seated body and base merge into chair/boot competitor; weaker than N124.
Horizontal base and merged upper silhouette can read seat/kettle; weaker human anatomy than N124.
Tread-like pattern without convincing wheel or damage state.
Ring/flat base retains camera/dial competitor; localized rupture not clear enough.
Hanging bracket/anchor competitor; steering blade not clear.
Central shaft/foot competitor; faulty underwater part without reliable rudder identity.
Oblique strokes read motion/speed, not uniquely acoustic cancellation.
Underwater oval plus signals plausible but weaker ship context than N133.
Entry/transfer/docking arrow competes with ingress, and water meaning is weak.
Swamping plausible but wave/ship relationships less clean than N138.

actualMaskDiversity.finding: All pairs have different actual native24 masks. Visual construction differences are visible: side versus frontal support poses, alternate seated leg/base configurations, sidewall versus tread views, stern/underhung/detached blade layouts, downward/lateral/submerged signal fields, and breach/side-profile/submerged hull treatments. Fatigue variants are the narrowest conceptual exploration; especially N124/N125 share the seated concept despite different legs. No claim that different hashes alone establish diversity.
actualMaskDiversity.quantitativeLimit: IoU and differing pixels are diagnostics, not a scoring threshold.

setChecks.contour: No new clipping or halo visible in inspected images; holes and large separations survive24. Ivory-on-light is low contrast and must not be used unbacked in gameplay.
setChecks.consistency: New pressure icons are relatively small; body/boat symbols denser. Reinspect final19 sheet; no optical-weight parity claim yet.
setChecks.scope: All20 inspected on native24/32 sheets over dark/light/checker, plus all20 native24 dark8x. No actual battlefield/distance testing.
setChecks.retained11: Existing canonical hashes independently verified unchanged before this review; current full-set review still required.
